description:
src/ir_interp/dispatch_exec.rs: DispatchExecState is HashMap<SubjectId, BackendBoundValue>, cloned whole at every DispatchNode::Test (:117) and at every Outcome, so a plan with k tests performs k map clones per decision; every cache hit clones a lane vector (:245, :302). The native lowering has the same shape (DispatchState::clone per Test in lower_dispatch_node) but pays it once per plan at compile time. About a quarter of interpreter samples on tail_recursion sit under execute_dispatch_node.

Subjects are dense ids (plan.matrix.subjects[id]). Every writer into the state is a pure resolution of (subject, operands), so entries carried across a miss are value-identical. The one non-obvious case is a bitstring shape that writes extracted field subjects and then fails (:781 then :787/:795) while dispatch_bit_size_value (:801-810) reads state for BitstringFieldSize::Binding.

Change: DispatchExecState becomes Vec<Option<BackendBoundValue>> sized by the plan's subject count plus an undo journal (Vec<SubjectId> of writes since the branch point; on miss, truncate and clear). Accessors return references so a cache hit no longer clones. Lines go up slightly; allocations go from one clone per Test node to one vector per run. The journal keeps the bitstring case closed by construction.

Signal: the bitstring fixtures (00309, 00326, 00339) and entry_dispatch_decides_a_lane_form_tuple_from_its_lanes on three doors; a unit test over a plan with nested tests asserting one state allocation per run.
title: Dispatch state is a dense vector with an undo journal; no clone per Test node
